_meta.purpose: Two things that make ~125 parallel wave-1 authoring agents safe: (A) one id-namespace prefix per partition, so an id collision is structurally impossible rather than merely detected; (B) the closed naming grammar and the collision-normalization algorithm that catches the thematic collisions a namespace cannot (Ashen Fang / Ash Fang / Fang of Ash / Ashfang).
_meta.consumedBy: ~125 wave-1a/1b authoring agents, plus the V1 validator (post-validation safety net) and F1 (reserved word pools, which this file hands a grammar to but does not itself populate).
_meta.immutability: FROZEN v1 once an owner flips `frozen` to true at the wave-0 freeze gate. After that: no prefix is reassigned, no partition's namespace shrinks, no naming pattern is added or removed in place. A change is v2, minted only after an explicit owner re-run decision.
_meta.doesNotOwn: The reserved word pools themselves (the actual adjective/noun/concept vocabularies authors draw from) belong to F1. This file specifies the SHAPE a word-pool entry must have for the collision algorithm in §3 to work (a canonical id plus tagged surface forms), and hands that shape to F1 — it does not populate a single word.

idPolicy.sequenceRule: The agent owns only this zero-padded 3-digit sequence, appended last inside its assigned prefix. It never touches the prefix, and it is never asked to check for collision with any other partition, because no other partition can produce the same prefix.

sequenceRange.note: 900-999 is reserved, in every single partition listed in idNamespaces, for later hand-authored corrections or additions to that same partition (seed-contract.md §7.2 'entry is a different thing now → new id'). No wave-1 agent may use 900-999. This reservation is uniform across all 125 partitions so a reviewer never has to look up a partition-specific rule.

idPolicy.neverReused: Once an id (in any namespace below) is minted, it is never reused — not after a deletion, not after a rejected review, not ever. A retired entry is disabled (`enabled: false`) with the file kept, per seed-contract.md §7.2. A reused id would silently repoint every reference that already resolved to it.
idPolicy.noDotInBody: Wherever a minted id doubles as (or feeds) a container_id — base types and, per the open question in §5 below, uniques and sets — the body after the first dot is `[a-z0-9-]+` with no second dot, per definitions.md §1's container_id grammar `^(item|trait|skill|species-passive|patron|world-buff)\.[a-z0-9-]+$`. Every template in idNamespaces below is hyphen-only after its leading `<kind>.` segment.

idNamespaces._readFirst: Every entry below names an idTemplate. `{seq:03}` is the agent's owned 3-digit sequence (001-899 for the wave-1 batch). Nothing else in a template is the agent's to choose — frame, role, band, theme, axis and slot tokens are all fixed by this file or by the sibling registries it cites.

idNamespaces._commanderStandardsRemoved: Removed wave 0c. A top-level group here was the wrong fix: the namespace expander is keyed by kind, and commander base types are kind base-type, so a group with no kind of its own could never be reached and instead reported itself uncovered. The expander now derives commander prefixes directly from core.v1.json roles.commanderOnly, single-banded. The allocation lives in code because it is derived, not authored — which is the same rule the rest of this contract applies to everything else.

patterns.why3: Three patterns cover every worked example read this session across I3 (base-type names), I8 §4.12 (prefix/suffix flavour words and the magic-item grammar), G1 (unique names — Thornmantle, Windforce-style), I5 (set names — Ember Legion), and I10 (charm names — Hardened Seedcase, Signet of the Hollow Crown), with zero residual case. A 4th 'combination' pattern is deliberately NOT offered to authors — see generatedOnlyPattern below — because offering it would let an author's hand-typed combination collide, un-detectably, with the one the engine already assembles from patterns 1+2. Closing the set at 3 is what keeps 'an author picks a pattern; it never invents one' true rather than aspirational.

list.description: Two space-separated words; the first modifies the second. The Base half is a noun realizing either a base-type's role-frame identity (e.g. 'Crown', 'Torc') or a unique/set/charm's own invented noun.
usedFor: the left half of a rolled magic-item name (I8 §4.12) — engine-assembled, not separately authored
list.example: Heartbloom Crown, Ember Legion, Hardened Seedcase

list.description: A Base noun, the literal connective 'of', and a Concept phrase (1-2 words, optionally itself prefixed with 'the' — see pluralsPossessivesConnectives). 'of' is the only preposition ever legal in an authored name.
usedFor: the suffix half of a rolled magic-item name (I8 §4.12's word table — 'of Embers', 'of the Wellspring') — engine-assembled when used for that purpose, hand-authored when it IS the whole unique/set name
list.example: Fang of Ash, Signet of the Hollow Crown

list.description: A single word formed by concatenating EXACTLY two known pool words with no separator and no internal case break. Restricted to exactly two, because the collision-normalization algorithm (§3 below) must be able to decompose it back into its two constituent words unambiguously — a fusion that does not decompose to exactly one known pair at authoring time is rejected before it ever reaches the corpus-wide collision check.
usedFor: unique names (the single most evocative slot)
occasionally a base-type or set name where a fused word reads better than two separate ones
list.example: Ashfang (= Ash + Fang), Thornmantle (= Thorn + Mantle)

generatedOnlyPattern.note: This is patterns 1+2 concatenated. It is what I8 §4.12's runtime naming function assembles for a Magic-rarity rolled instance ('Sturdy Bark Helm of Embers') from the item's own highest-tier prefix word and highest-tier suffix word. No author ever types this shape directly as a `name` field — an author who wants an unusually elaborate unique/set name picks pattern 'compound' or 'of-construct' for two SEPARATE fields (or accepts a shorter name) rather than hand-typing the combined shape, precisely so the collision check in §3 (which runs over every authored `name`) never has to reconcile a hand-typed 4-part name against an engine-assembled one of the same shape.

pluralsPossessivesConnectives.plurals: Forbidden in every identity name (base type, unique, set, charm `name` field). An item template names one specific thing; pluralising it implies a category, which is `nameKey`'s job, not `name`'s. Flavour-text prose is exempt — it is free text per seed-contract.md §6 and is not run through this grammar at all.
pluralsPossessivesConnectives.possessives: Forbidden — no `'s`. Two reasons, both structural: (1) an apostrophe is exactly the kind of decoration collision-normalization strips (seed-contract.md §5 step 2), so 'Dragon Fang' and 'Dragon's Fang' already normalize identically — allowing the possessive form would teach authors a name shape the corpus's own dedup logic treats as fake variation; (2) it is one more character class the normalizer's punctuation-stripping step has to handle correctly for zero benefit.
pluralsPossessivesConnectives.invatedConnectives: Forbidden. The only connective words a name may ever contain are `of` and, immediately following it, optionally `the` — and only inside the 'of-construct' pattern (`<Base> of <Concept>` or `<Base> of the <Concept>`). No other connective (`and`, `from`, `at`, `upon`, `&`, a hyphenated compound acting as a connective) may appear in an authored `name`. This is what keeps the dropped-word list in §3 below closed at exactly four entries forever — an author who invents a fifth connective breaks the normalizer's completeness guarantee, not just their own file.

collisionNormalization.purpose: Reserved word pools (F1's, not this file's) stop THEMATIC collision — two authors both reaching for 'fire' words. They do not stop the SAME idea being spelled four different ways. This algorithm catches that, deterministically, at import — never left to a reviewer's eye.
algorithm: 2. Tokenize on whitespace and punctuation boundaries (space, hyphen, apostrophe, comma) into surface tokens. A 'fusion'-pattern word with no internal boundary is split into its exactly-two constituent pool words instead (this is exactly why pattern 'fusion' is capped at two words — the split must be unambiguous, and it is checked at authoring time, not guessed at comparison time).

2a. WHOLE-TOKEN RESOLUTION PRECEDES FUSION DECOMPOSITION. Before splitting any token, test the whole token against the registered canonical ids and surface forms in words.v1.json. If it resolves as a whole, it is atomic and is NEVER decomposed. Only an unresolved token is a fusion candidate. Without this an atomic seed such as Thistledown decomposes into unrelated halves and collides with names that share neither idea. Added during wave 0b after F1 hit the case while building the pools.

3. Resolve every surface token to its RESERVED-WORD-POOL CANONICAL ID via that word's registered surface forms. A word's canonical id is invariant across the pattern-slot it appears in — e.g. if F1's pool registers canonical id `ash` with surface forms {noun: 'Ash', adjective: 'Ashen'}, then both 'Ash' (used as a noun in a fusion or an of-construct) and 'Ashen' (used as an adjective in a compound) resolve to `ash`. A surface token with no pool entry at all (an ordinary base-type noun like 'Crown', not a pool flavour word) resolves to itself, lowercased, as its own canonical id.
4. Drop any resolved token that is one of the four closed connectives: `of`, `the`, `a`, `and`. This is the complete list — see invatedConnectives above for why it can never grow.
5. Sort the remaining canonical ids, ordinal (byte) comparison, ascending.

6. Compare the sorted canonical-id list against every other authored name's sorted list, corpus-wide (not per category, not per partition — see nameKey.globalUniqueness below for the identical rule applied to keys). An exact match rejects every entry but the first one authored, tiebroken by `_meta.authoredUtc` then by id ordinal.
collisionNormalization.wordPoolShapeRequiredForThisToWork: F1's reserved word pools must register each entry as {canonicalId, surfaceForms: {noun?, adjective?, ofConcept?}} rather than a flat list of interchangeable strings — the noun/adjective surface-form split is what lets step 3 collapse 'Ashen' onto 'ash'. This is the one shape requirement this file hands to F1; F1 still owns every actual word.
collisionNormalization.wordPoolDisjointnessIsSeparate: F1 additionally partitions WHICH canonical ids go to which consuming partition, so two volume agents never reach for the same flavour word at all (thematic collision). That is orthogonal to this algorithm: F1's partitioning prevents two authors from typing 'Ember' in the first place; this algorithm catches the case where two authors, independently and legally, produce names that mean the same thing through different legal patterns.
collisionNormalization.wave0RejectionCodeNote: A `NameCollision` reason code does not exist in definitions.md §10's closed list of 33. Registering it (or folding it into an existing collision-shaped code, per the `ContentRuleViolated` option ssot-uniques.md §6.3 already raises for its own six-code ask) is a request to whoever owns that list next, not a decision this file makes.

workedExample.assumedPoolEntry: canonical id `ash` → surfaceForms {noun: 'Ash', adjective: 'Ashen'}; canonical id `fang` → surfaceForms {noun: 'Fang'}
workedExample.result: All four sort to the identical canonical key ['ash', 'fang']. Whichever was authored first (by `_meta.authoredUtc`) stands; the other three reject.

collisionNormalization.wholeTokenRuleNote: Rule 2a is load-bearing for uniqueSetSeedPools, whose entries are deliberately atomic compounds. The validator must implement 2a exactly or seed names will false-positive against ordinary two-word names.

nameKey.recommendedFormat: <kindPrefix>.<slug>, matching seed-contract.md's own examples exactly: base.heartbloom-crown, unique.thornmantle, affix.elemental-power, set.ember-legion.
nameKey.slugRule: slug = lowercase(name), spaces and apostrophes → hyphens, all other punctuation stripped, repeated hyphens collapsed to one.
nameKey.globalUniqueness: `nameKey` is unique across the ENTIRE corpus, not per kind and not per partition (seed-contract.md §6 states this explicitly). `base.ember-crown` and `unique.ember-crown` collide even though they are different kinds — a slug derived independently by two different partitions is exactly the case the corpus-wide check must catch, because nothing in the id namespaces above stops two unrelated authors from independently naming two different things 'Ember Crown'.
nameKey.disambiguationRule: If an author's slug collides with an existing nameKey, the fix is to append the author's OWN partition token (already unique, per idNamespaces above) to the slug — e.g. `unique.ember-crown-thorned-chassis` — never to silently pick a near-miss spelling, which is exactly the failure collisionNormalization exists to catch on the `name` side too. The V1 validator is the safety net that catches an author who does not do this.

perFrameNaming.rule: The same role is `head-guard` (frame-neutral role id, invisible to players) on both frames, `head` on humanoid and `crown` on plant (core.v1.json → roles.list). Naming interacts with this in exactly one place and must not leak it anywhere else.
whatChanges: The noun realizing the role in pattern 'compound' or as the Base of 'of-construct' — 'Heartbloom Crown' (plant) vs the humanoid equivalent for the same role, e.g. 'Heartbloom Helm'. This noun comes from I3's base-type record / F4's class ladder, not from this file.

Which word-pool surface form applies, where I8 §4.12's `word_plant` override column is populated — a family's flavour word may differ by frame (e.g. band-C `quickening` reads 'Quickening' on humanoid, 'Blooming' on plant) precisely because a rooted, handless body cannot 'quicken' the way a humanoid can (ssot-equip-slots.md §2.6's possession test).
whatDoesNotChange: The pattern selected. An author does not invent a plant-specific pattern — the same 3 patterns in §2 above apply on both frames.
The role_id used for game logic (`effect_container.slot`, `effect_binding.slot`) — it is always the frame-neutral id, never a display word, per ssot-equip-slots.md §2.2.
Frame-neutral flavour words (most of I8 §4.12's word table works on both frames unchanged, e.g. 'Sturdy', 'Ember', 'of the Wellspring').

The collision-normalization algorithm. Frame is invisible to it by design: 'Ember Crown' and 'Ember Helm' contain different canonical Base tokens (`crown` vs `helm`), so they correctly do NOT collide — they are different items worn by different bodies, and the algorithm must never merge them.

handoffToF1.whatThisFileFixed: Three authored name-construction patterns (compound, of-construct, fusion); the closed 4-word connective list (of, the, a, and); the ban on plurals and possessives; the collision-normalization algorithm and the canonical-id/surface-form shape a word-pool entry must have for that algorithm to work; and — separately, in idNamespaces — every partition's id prefix.
handoffToF1.whatF1MustProduce: The actual reserved word pools: for every consuming partition (base types by role×frame per ssot-equip-slots.md's own note that naming inherits it, affix families' flavour words per I8 §4.12's word table, unique/set/charm names per their assigned theme), a disjoint set of pool entries shaped as {canonicalId, surfaceForms: {noun?, adjective?, ofConcept?}}. F1's disjointness (no two partitions sharing a word) is a DIFFERENT safety net from this file's id-namespace disjointness (no two partitions sharing a prefix) and from collisionNormalization (catching the same idea spelled four ways) — all three run together, none substitutes for another.

openAmbiguities: Uniques/sets — id vs container_id. This file's `unique.{...}` and `set.{...}` ids are the authored seed-corpus tracking namespace (matching seed-contract.md §4's own worked examples). Neither prefix is in definitions.md §1's container_id alternation as written; ssot-uniques.md §3.4 and ssot-sets.md §4.3 both describe the underlying DB row as `container_kind = 'item'` (unique) or a `set`-kind tier container with a DIFFERENT id shape (`set.{set_id}-{pieces:D2}`, no separate 'unique'/'set' alternation needed once `set` joins per ssot-sets.md §9's ask). The exact function from this file's authored `id` to the eventual `container_id` is not specified in anything read this session and should be confirmed before wave-1b (uniques/sets) authoring starts, not assumed by an agent mid-batch.
